Cross‑dataset redundant‑readout evidence: Exp017 (TwoLeadECG): redundant 3‑head reduced logit MAE and increased Q.ANT accuracy.
Exp018 (GunPoint): redundant 3‑head reduced logit MAE, slight increase in disagreements (floor effect).
Exp019 (SonyAIBORobotSurface1): redundant 3‑head reduced logit MAE, unchanged accuracy.

analysis: The promotion experiment (Exp020) demonstrated that adding three independent Q.ANT‑native readouts and averaging logits improves mean absolute logit error (0.0200 vs 0.0326) while preserving or slightly increasing aggregate Q.ANT correct predictions (897 vs 893). Subsequent compression attempts (Exp021) showed that a heavily compressed 4,278‑parameter version loses 10 correct predictions (887) and, although logit error improves, the aggregate‑correct gate fails. Across three datasets, redundant readout consistently lowers logit MAE without harming accuracy, suggesting the readout design is a robust numerical‑agreement intervention. The next logical variable is the size of the local window representation (currently a fixed 16‑dimensional output per window). Reducing this dimensionality could lower total parameters below the 8,550 of Alpha5 while retaining the redundant readout benefits, addressing the compression limitation observed in Exp021.
hypothesis: Reducing the dimensionality of the per‑window local representation from 16 to a narrower width (e.g., 8 or 12) while keeping the three‑head redundant readout will maintain or improve the aggregate Q.ANT correct count (≥ 897/1000) and keep mean absolute logit error ≤ 0.02001, thereby achieving a smaller model (< 8,000 parameters) without sacrificing the numerical‑agreement gains of the redundant readout.

proposal.title: PNN‑v1‑Proposal022 – Narrow‑Window Representation with Redundant Readout
proposal.research_question: Can a reduced‑width local representation (≤ 12 dimensions) preserve the promoted Alpha5 performance metrics while decreasing total parameter count below 8,000?
proposal.rationale: Exp020 proved the redundant readout improves logit agreement. Exp021 showed that aggressive compression of the whole model (including readout) harms aggregate accuracy. By targeting only the local representation for size reduction, we aim to achieve genuine compression without losing the readout‑driven robustness.

procedure: Train each candidate on the ECG200 training set using the same hyper‑parameters as Exp020.
Evaluate on the ECG200 test set with 5 random seeds.
Record aggregate correct predictions (sum over seeds) and mean absolute logit error (average over seeds).

success_criteria.decision_rule: If any candidate satisfies all three gates, the experiment is classified as supported and the winning candidate becomes the new active model.

risks: Reduced local width may cause a drop in aggregate correct predictions below the 897 threshold.
Training variance across seeds could obscure small differences; multiple seeds are required.
Simulation runtime may increase with multiple candidates; budget caps mitigate this.
